tagline: Two passes, the Carson River, then Tahoe's west shore.
intro: From US 395 near Topaz, Highway 89 works west through a few switchbacks and climbs to Monitor Pass at 8,314 feet, then comes down to the Carson River at Markleeville and Woodfords. It climbs once more, over Luther Pass at 7,740 feet, drops toward Lake Tahoe at Meyers and runs up the lake's west shore past Camp Richardson and Emerald Bay.

The pavement over Monitor Pass came late, finished in the early 1950s, one of the last Sierra passes to get a paved road. The way itself is old. Jedediah Smith came through it in 1827, on the first crossing of the Sierra Nevada by a non-native.

moments.title: Markleeville
moments.text: The county seat stands on the claim of Jacob Marklee, who put a toll bridge across the Carson River in 1861 and died after a gunfight two years later.

moments.title: Woodfords
moments.text: Warren Upson rode in over Luther Pass through a blinding snowstorm in April 1860 to open the Pony Express station here, and five weeks later the route moved elsewhere.

moments.title: Emerald Bay
moments.text: On the shore stands Vikingsholm, a 38-room summer house built in 1929, and out on Fannette Island, the only island in Lake Tahoe, its owner kept a tea house.

practical: Monitor Pass is closed by snow each winter. The dates vary with the weather, but it is generally shut from late November to early April.
